name: Kickback
why: Big flat gain with a small gift you aim; the gift is a mild kingmaking nudge, nothing builds from it.

name: Golden Years
why: Pure flat 2/4/6 income; nobody at the table notices who took it.

name: Intro Offer
why: A strong, clear discount that shapes your next buy, but a cost cut says nothing about gold.

name: Collect Debts
why: Aimed steal of gold you can point at the leader or the hoarder; real targeting choice.

name: Tithe
why: Scales with your cult so it rewards building, but it is quiet income nobody reacts to.

name: Double Down
why: A big round III burst for the gold leader and dead for everyone else.

name: Banker
why: Steady +3 gold income at 9 total cost; reliable but flat and invisible to rivals.

name: Prospector
why: +1 gold on gold gains: a small trigger that never feels like a moment.

name: Tax Collector
why: Costs 9 to collect +1 gold when rivals buy followers; a rarely meaningful trickle.

name: Merchant
why: +1 gold when anyone recruits a gold member; narrow and forgettable.

name: Penny Pincher
why: Doubling gold spent on members bends the price rule and makes gold planning matter; unclear whether it covers the any part.

name: Underdog
hardFail: relies on a rival having more gold than you
why: Doubling gains while behind is a real comeback but the condition is a rival holding more gold.

name: Alchemists
hardFail: plural name on a single member (worth 1)
why: +1 gold whenever an action gives another color: a dull +1, and the name is plural for one body; shares a name with the guest card.

name: Speculator
why: A once-per-game doubling with good timing tension, but it is Double Down on a card.

name: Tycoon
why: Game-end gold to followers at half rate; a mild reason to hold that fights the follower buy.

name: Treasurer
why: Pays more the later you buy it, a clean timing choice, but no one else feels it.

name: Envy
hardFail: relies on a rival having more gold than you
why: Catch-up income that only exists if a rival out-hoards you; the minus math reads awkwardly.

name: Tryout
why: Borrowing a shop member's On Recruit without buying it is a fresh angle that makes the shop row matter.

name: Gather
why: Scaling red plus a recruit bonus; a fine anchor that nobody reacts to.

name: Walk-In
why: A blind free recruit is a gamble the table watches; the gift to rivals is a small cost.

name: Promote
why: Trading up into a rival's better member is a sting, a plan and a real choice of target.

name: Demote
why: Trading down for red and a cheaper rival member; a choice with a sting, weaker than its twin.

name: Initiation
why: A free member up to 8 is a satisfying round III burst everyone recognises.

name: Triplets
why: Three bodies for 3 is a plain efficient body that feeds member-count cards.

name: Body Snatchers
why: A round-start swap with a rival every round is a recurring sting and a target.

name: Volunteer
why: One follower for one red; filler with no moment.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: A two-for-one recruit that feels big, though the cheapest shop member is often junk.

name: Proselytizers
why: A follower per recruit builds with red's free recruits but is quiet.

name: Mob
why: A big round-end payout tied to red member counts; strong engine but it rewards the leader.

name: Recruiter
why: +1 red per recruit; a forgettable trickle.

name: Host
why: Red income that scales with cult size; per-2 math is mildly fiddly and invisible to rivals.

name: Patriarch
why: A member-count scorer that rewards wide cults; quiet.

name: Greeters
why: 'Your On Recruits also give +1 of that color' is an odd small bonus that rarely registers.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Four bodies for 3 plus a sting on red swaps; nearly a must-buy at this price.

name: Panel
why: A free promote or demote on arrival turns an old member into a better one; strong red engine piece.

name: Loyalists
why: Protection from swaps is a visible block that answers Red and Body Snatchers.

name: Headhunter
why: Breaks a rival's engine piece, but giving them an equal or pricier card is a strange reward to read.

name: Clerk
why: Round Start +1 red for 5 total: the dullest card here, nothing to plan or notice.

name: Sleep In
why: Big purple for going last; the Goes Last token creates a visible tradeoff and feeds Night Watch.

name: Hold Up
why: Skipping whoever is next, even yourself, is a sting with real timing thought.

name: Right Away
why: Simple tempo: take a contested space before rivals react.

name: Last Call
why: Followers for minions you hold back plus the Goes Last token; a clear timing bet.

name: Crunch Time
why: Three placements in a row is a powerful grab the table feels.

name: Overtime
why: An extra minion with some purple; solid round III burst but mostly net zero.

name: Go-Getter
why: A once-per-game extra minion right now; clean, felt and timed.

name: Late Risers
why: An extra early minion for the player behind; a genuine catch-up rule bend.

name: Courier
why: Rewards double turns with a rainbow; combos with snake ends and Crunch Time but nobody else feels it.

name: Clockmakers
why: Two first turns in a row each round is a reliable, readable rule bend.

name: Night Watch
why: Pays only when a rival takes Goes Last; narrow and rarely aimed.

name: Night Owls
why: An extra minion each round from II; strong but expensive and leader-friendly.

name: Early Birds
why: Immunity to skips is a visible block against Hold Up and Bouncers.

name: Bouncers
why: Skipping the next two rivals on arrival is a clear sting with timing choice.

name: Pocket Watch
why: Cheap payoff for skips that ties purple's skip cards together.

name: Gossip
why: A follower per skip, a sibling of Pocket Watch that pays a bit better.

name: Extra Shift
why: Nine resources for one extra minion once; worse than Go-Getter in every way.

name: Timekeeper
why: Generic per-color-member scorer; quiet.

name: Closer
why: +4 purple for placing the round's last minion; a small turn-order race.

name: Hot Streak
why: Rewards stacking in-a-row turns with a big payoff you can set up.

name: Shift Crew
why: Four followers for 4 resources: a vanilla must-buy with nothing to it.

name: Night Shift
hardFail: needs tracking a table can't do (whether a minion was placed before the skip)
why: Unreadable chain of conditions; no table could say what happens before choosing it.

name: Toast
why: A big silver gain that gifts every rival; scaled and on theme.

name: Polish
why: A plain converter; useful, unnoticed.

name: Party Gifts
why: Followers for gifts with a split you choose; the core silver tension in one space.

name: Potluck
why: Each rival gives their least useful resource, so the choice is fake, but the exchange is felt.

name: Sweet Talk
why: Silver into other colors; a converter that nobody notices.

name: Largesse
why: A big gift-for-followers burst that hands rivals contest silver; strong round III tension.

name: Hangers-On
why: +1 more of every gift; pays only when rivals choose to give, which they avoid.

name: Godparent
why: Give a member away for its cost in followers; a gift with a payoff and a combo with Old Maid and Martyrs.

name: Gift Wrapper
why: +1 follower on each give; small add-on to the silver spaces.

name: Hostesses
why: A gift every round that pays you per rival; recurring and on theme.

name: Caterer
why: +1 silver whenever silver is gifted; a minor trickle.

name: Toastmaster
why: Cheap follower per silver space; good value but forgettable.

name: Debutantes
why: Once-per-game doubling with a gift; a felt moment.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: Silver as a wild color frees the economy, but costs 11 and is invisible to rivals.

name: Philanthropist
why: A smaller Largesse on recruit; adds no new angle.

name: Polisher
why: A once-per-game converter; dull.

name: Collector
why: +1 silver when rivals pay silver; rarely fires.

name: Creditor
why: Every round take 2 followers from a rival you choose and pay them silver; aimed, stinging, on theme.

name: Debt Collectors
why: A one-shot tax on rivals; taking is off-theme for a giving color.

name: High Society
why: Pays when rivals take silver spaces; a passive tax with nothing to decide.

name: Harvest
why: Flexible colored income; solid and quiet.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reads the board to pick a color; a real choice that cares where rivals went.

name: New Blood
why: Rewards a new color in your cult; a clear pull toward variety.

name: Big New Blood
why: A bigger New Blood; strong but a sibling.

name: Melting Pot
why: Pays a varied cult; an engine payoff nobody else feels.

name: Makeover
why: Round III rearrange; useful for contests but a weak burst.

name: Gardener
hardFail: singular name on a member that counts as 2
why: Tops up missing colors each round; a mild catch-up, but the name doesn't match its two bodies.

name: Customs Officer
why: +1 yellow when rivals steal or change your stuff; a small consolation.

name: Go-Between
why: Change one resource per space; a small convenience.

name: Tourist
why: A follower per color held, each round; a strong visible engine of variety.

name: Tinker
why: Swap up to 3 resources one for one with no clear partner; fiddly and small.

name: Harmonist
why: Full sets at game end; hard to read at a glance.

name: Matchmaker
why: Rewards a new color each recruit; combos with New Blood.

name: Dyer
why: Yellow per color held; quiet income.

name: Meddler
why: Change each rival's resource and gain per rival; contest interference the table notices.

name: Drifters
why: Picks its own color, feeding count cards and New Blood; quiet but flexible.

name: Leveler
why: Every round shave each rival's biggest pile into a color you name; contest disruption aimed at leaders.

name: Big Tent
why: Two followers per color with one member; a clear build-wide plan.

name: Book Cookers
why: Makeover on a member; nothing new.

name: Caravan
why: A rainbow each round; solid but quiet.

name: Tastemaker
why: +1 follower when you change rivals' resources; a small add-on.

name: Spice Route
why: Game end per color with 3 or more; pulls against spending.

name: Guest Book
why: Cheap +2 yellow on new colors; efficient but forgettable.

name: Savings
why: Scaling blue plus an optional bury; fine anchor.

name: Out of Style
why: Wiping a color from the shop denies rivals and pays you; a visible board play.

name: Peek
why: Stacking the pile and recruiting from it is a planning tool unique to blue.

name: Recruit Twice
why: Two buys in one turn is the late-game bottleneck broken.

name: Bury
why: Hate-bury a member a rival wants and get paid; a clean block.

name: Spree
why: Three recruits is the round III burst; leader-friendly.

name: Connoisseurs
why: +1 blue per blue recruit; a small trickle.

name: Hawker
why: An auction where rivals pay you or you get it free; everyone at the table decides.

name: Bargain Bin
why: Cheap trickle off any bury; ties blue's spaces together but never a moment.

name: Patroness
why: Follower per bury; a pricier Bargain Bin.

name: Snobs
why: Generic blue-member scorer.

name: Window Shopper
why: Bury two and take their colors each round; unclear whether the row refills.

name: Restockers
why: Flush the whole shop once; a big denial moment.

name: Shopaholics
why: Two buys every turn is a huge engine for whoever is already rich.

name: Window Dressers
why: Three bodies plus a three-card bury; efficient and mildly disruptive.

name: Plus-Ones
why: A recruit that pays back its recruit; strong and clean.

name: Doormen
why: Bounce a rival's member and hand them another; a sting, but the 'any amount more' half reads oddly.

name: Regular
why: +1 blue per follower buy; dull.

name: Trendsetters
why: Three bodies and a bury per recruit; steady shop pressure.

name: Critic
why: Follower when rivals take blue members; passive.

name: Scavenger
why: Grab what rivals bury, out of turn; turns their denial against them.

name: Help Yourself
why: Scaling aimed theft; the core of magenta and a catch-up tool.

name: Stash
why: Same shape as Gather and Allowance; no magenta angle.

name: Lie Low
why: Steal a little and go untouchable; a visible defensive play.

name: Heist
why: Three followers from a rival you pick; a direct sting.

name: Shake Down
why: The rival picks between paying and losing a member; a real two-sided choice.

name: Poach
why: Take any rival's member free; the round III punch.

name: Cutpurse
why: Cheap steady theft from the richest; mild catch-up.

name: Accomplice
why: Cheap three-steal on arrival; good value, one moment.

name: Grifter
why: Scaling steal on recruit; expensive for one hit.

name: Sticky Fingers
why: Every steal bigger; the plain magenta engine piece.

name: Second-Story Man
why: A pre-contest steal every round swings rims; aimed and felt.

name: Desperado
why: Bigger steals while behind; a true comeback card.

name: Robin Hood
why: Rewards hitting the leader; catch-up with a small payoff.

name: Extortionist
why: A bigger Cutpurse at triple the price; no new angle.

name: Bodyguards
why: Theft immunity is a clear block but shuts out interaction.

name: Crew
why: Two bodies for 3; vanilla.

name: Double Agent
why: Trade this card for a rival's; the value of what you give is hard to read.

name: Fixer
why: Buy a rival's member with magenta once; a planned sting.

name: Kingpin
why: Generic magenta-member scorer.

name: Kidnapper
why: Take the widest cult's cheapest member every round; recurring pressure on the leader in bodies.

name: Snitch
why: A deterrent that makes stealing from you cost; felt by thieves.

name: Shoplifter
why: A steal per recruit; small and automatic.

name: Fence
why: Paid when robbed; a defensive sibling of Snitch.

name: Allowance
why: Same shape as Gather and Stash; no white angle.

name: Splurge
why: Followers for paying big; unclear about round III, but a strong spend payoff.

name: Exchange
why: Resources into followers at double rate; the white idea in its cleanest form.

name: Farewell
why: Cash a member out for its cost; a real decision with combos.

name: Estate Sale
why: Farewell for white instead of followers; weaker twin.

name: Cash In
why: All white into followers; the burst the color builds toward.

name: Recluse
why: Rewards a small cult; a different plan that pays the player with fewer members.

name: Landlord
why: Cheap +2 white each round; good value, quiet.

name: Heiresses
why: Once-per-game white per member; small for 9.

name: Brokers
why: Three bodies plus a follower on white actions; efficient support.

name: Exporters
why: +1 white on off-color recruits; trickle.

name: Misers
why: Game-end white scorer; quiet.

name: Raiders
why: A four-follower steal is a big sting, but theft belongs to magenta.

name: Cashier
why: A Cash In on a member; strong timing choice, not new.

name: Undertaker
why: Pays for casting out; ties Farewell and Estate Sale together.

name: Money Changers
why: +1 white whenever anyone buys followers; passive trickle.

name: Martyrs
why: Pays when it leaves, so stealing it hurts the thief; great combo with Farewell and Godparent.

name: Old Money
why: Generic white-member scorer.

name: Hoarder
why: Everything into white once; a contest swing with timing.

name: Build Up
why: Flat scaling green; nothing to react to.

name: Echo
why: Copying the previous action scales with what rivals just took; the color's best idea.

name: Reprise
why: Copy your own action; self-contained.

name: Sample
why: Use a rival's member's On Recruit; reaches into other cults.

name: Cover
why: Copy an open space; flexible and reads the board.

name: Greatest Hits
why: Re-fire every On Recruit; a payoff you build all game.

name: Busker
why: Cheap steady green; fine value, quiet.

name: Muse
why: +1 green when rivals copy; rarely matters.

name: Impersonator
why: Borrow any rival's ability each round; big, aimed, and makes rivals' cards targets.

name: Understudy
why: Copy last turn's action on arrival; timing choice, one moment.

name: Ensemble
why: Three bodies and follower on self-copies; efficient.

name: Impressionist
why: +1 of the color on any copy; trickle.

name: Wallflower
why: Double copied resources; a real engine but pricey and private.

name: Fan Club
why: Copy a space the leader holds; catches you up and reads the board.

name: Roadie
why: Green per green member; quiet engine.

name: Stunt Double
why: Copy your own just-taken action; a sibling of Understudy.

name: Tribute Band
why: Do every action a rival took this round; a huge moment at a huge price.

name: Doppelganger
why: Copy your best member; strong but private.

name: Impostors
why: Copy a rival's member; reaches across the table.

name: Agents
why: Blocks copies; a clear counter.

name: Bait
why: Punishes copiers and pays you; a felt trap.

name: Chronicler
why: Generic green-member scorer.

name: Party Crasher
why: Take a space someone already has; breaks the blocking rule once, everyone feels it.

name: Big Spender
why: One extra buy once; cheap and quiet.

name: Alchemists
why: Resources count as any when recruiting; strong for 5 but unclear about colored parts.

name: Extra Hand
why: Nine for a once-per-game minion; overpriced.

name: Line Cutters
why: Three bodies for 2 that override the catch-up turn order; a must-buy that helps the leader.

name: Launderers
why: Rearrange on arrival with three bodies; good value, quiet.

name: Old Maid
why: A card built to be dumped on rivals; a sting with Godparent, Promote and Double Agent.

name: Dabblers
why: Two wild bodies for 3; feeds every count card, but 'wild' needs a ruling.

name: Cheerleader
why: +1 per contest won; trivial next to the prize.

name: Anarchist
why: Swap any two members anywhere each round; chaos the table watches.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancel a contest you can't win; a block every rim leader fears.

name: Con Men
why: A five-resource steal on arrival; a big moment, nothing after.

name: Coach
why: Free extra On Use; strong with once-per-game cards, private.

name: Sore Loser
why: Takes from the contest leader when you're shut out; real catch-up.

name: Tiebreaker
why: Win every tie; makes contest math matter.
